questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose to live in Denmark but study in Lund, so it was important that it was close to Copenhagen and therefore easy to travel to. Lund is also a highly ranked university that offers excellent study opportunities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Lund sent many emails upon my arrival, making it easy to find all the information I needed. They also responded quickly to emails, and everything ran smoothly. This was greatly appreciated and very different from my first exchange experience.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: As I didn’t live in Lund, I didn’t use their arrival assistance. However, I know that there were student ambassadors at the airport and various train stations, as well as support available upon arrival. From what I heard from other exchange students, this system worked very well.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I stayed in Copenhagen, but went to the lectures in Lund.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you want to commute from Denmark, the train usually works very well.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Although some things were a bit unclear on the website, they provided helpful videos.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The application was submitted through a portal, after which you had to rank the available courses in order of preference.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Videos and guides.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all my first choices.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: As a sociology student, I was a bit surprised by how few specific sociology courses were offered to master's students during the spring semester. In my case, no sociology courses were available. While there were several interdisciplinary master's courses, the overall range of options was not very broad.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I chose the inter disciplinary master courses. I took one statistics course, which I would say was at a very high level. However, overall, I found the courses to be easier than those in Copenhagen. Although there was more required attendance, or make-up assignments if you missed a class, and more continuous work throughout the course (due to the block structure, with only one course at a time), the exams were generally easier.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Overall, the experience was very similar. The teachers were addressed by their first names, and there was generally a sense that you could always approach and talk to them.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Critical Feminist Perspectives in Social Theory (15 ECTS)
2. Process Tracing (7.5 ECTS)
3. Quantitative Methods - Multivariate Analysis (7.5 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
If you're interested in learning Swedish, I know that Lund offers a popular Swedish course.

I didn’t enjoy the course Critical Feminist Perspectives in Social Theory as much. I found some aspects of it to be quite biased, and a significant amount of time was spent on seminars where students presented sessions that were sometimes not well planned. Additionally, I wasn’t convinced by the use of process tracing, which I didn't find to be well presented. That said, this is just my personal experience, and others may have found it more valuable.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: As I was living in Copenhagen, my experience reflects that. However, the Øresund travel card was quite expensive (around 2,000 DKK per month). I used most of my Erasmus grant to cover this cost. Some Danish students who were permanently studying there were able to get an 'Ungdomskort'.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Almost everything in Sweden is a bit cheaper than in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are many student nations offering various activities, and I think it's a great idea to join one.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Participate in the nations activities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit Malmö and explore the city and the harbor area. Also visit Kulturen in Lund.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy as I'm Danish and the Swedish culture is very similiar.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not any in particular.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I was impressed by how well-organized the university was, not only when it came to getting documents signed, but also in terms of how the Canvas platform was structured.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Check how many courses are available within your field of study.
2. Be aware that many courses require attendance, and if you miss a class, you may need to complete make-up assignments.
3. Although there are more assignments throughout the course, the final exams are often shorter, especially take-home written exams.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The above covers most.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I think it's always a great experience to study at another university and see how they approach academic teaching. It really broadens your horizons.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Time passed so quickly, and suddenly my exchange was over. Since it was winter during the first months, I forgot to take the time to enjoy the city. Toward the end, I had a more demanding course, and before I knew it, my exchange was over.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
